description: Source file implementing the DisplayOzone class for ANGLE's Ozone backend, handling EGL display initialization, buffer management, rendering, and presentation on Linux with DRM and GBM.

classes.name: SwapControlData
classes.description: Structure for swap interval control, currently unused.

classes.name: DisplayOzone
classes.description: Class implementing EGL display for Ozone backend, managing buffers, rendering, and presentation.

classes.name: Buffer
classes.description: Represents a buffer with GBM and DRM, handling creation, resizing, and texture binding.

classes.name: WorkerContextOzone
classes.description: Worker thread EGL context for background operations.

methods.name: chooseMode
methods.description: Selects preferred display mode from DRM connector.

methods.name: ChooseCRTC
methods.description: Selects CRTC index compatible with connector.

methods.name: hasUsableScreen
methods.description: Checks if a DRM device has an active connected screen.

methods.name: initialize
methods.description: Initializes the EGL display, sets up DRM, GBM, and EGL context.

methods.name: pageFlipHandler
methods.description: Handles page flip events for display refresh.

methods.name: presentScreen
methods.description: Schedules buffer presentation on the display.

methods.name: makeShader
methods.description: Compiles a GLSL shader of given type.

methods.name: drawWithTexture
methods.description: Draws a buffer texture onto the screen using shaders.

methods.name: drawBuffer
methods.description: Prepares and draws a buffer, then presents it.

methods.name: flushGL
methods.description: Flushes GL commands and optionally waits for fences.

methods.name: terminate
methods.description: Cleans up resources and shuts down display.

methods.name: createWindowSurface
methods.description: Creates a window surface with a buffer.

methods.name: createContext
methods.description: Creates an EGL context sharing renderer.

methods.name: createWorkerContext
methods.description: Creates a background worker EGL context.
